generalAbilities.name: Camouflage
generalAbilities.description: The assassin vine can Hide in natural environments even if it doesn't have cover.

defensiveAbilities.name: Alchemical Resistance
defensiveAbilities.description: An alchemist ivy takes 5 less damage from attacks with the alchemical trait.

defensiveAbilities.name: Chemical Fertilizer
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger A creature within 10 feet of the alchemist ivy Activates or is hit by an item with the alchemical trait

Effect The alchemist ivy briefly extends tendrils toward the creature and absorbs some of the alchemical residue, regaining 2d8 Healing Damage Hit Points and gaining a +15-foot status bonus to its Speed until the end of its next turn.

Effect: Chemical Fertilizer

defensiveAbilities.name: Grasping Foliage
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger The assassin vine detects a creature within 20 feet via Tremorsense

Effect The assassin vine causes vegetation within a 20ft Emanation to writhe for 1 round, turning this area into difficult terrain. When a creature starts its turn in this area, it must attempt a DC 20 Reflex Saving Throw save. On a failure, it takes a -10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it leaves the area, and on a critical failure it is also Immobilized for 1 round. A creature can attempt to Escape to remove these effects.

Assassin vines are immune to Grasping Foliage.

offensiveAbilities.name: Constrict
offensiveAbilities.description:
(1d8+4) Bludgeoning Damage, Basic DC 20 Fortitude Saving Throw

See rules...

The monster deals the listed amount of damage to any number of creatures Grabbed or Restrained by it. Each of those creatures can attempt a basic Fortitude save with the listed DC.

offensiveAbilities.name: Grab
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.
